Supporting foundation: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution. Supporting lemma: Underlying equivalences and operadic colimits of coherent modules. Supporting step: Coherent modules as inert-preserving simplicial sections. Operadic meaning of coherent left-tensoring and modules.

title: Operadic encoding of a coherent left tensoring
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, nerves, mapping spaces, full subcategories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In this node a categorical fibration is an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with prescribed source.

Write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ for finite pointed sets. Define the ordinary category $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ as follows. An object is $(\langle n\rangle,S)$ with $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$; indices in $S$ have colour $m$, the others colour $a$. A morphism to $(\langle k\rangle,T)$ is a pointed map $f:\langle n\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$ and a linear order on each $f^{-1}(j)$ for $j\ne *$, subject to: $f(S)\subseteq T\cup\{*\}$, and for each $j\in T$, $f^{-1}(j)$ contains exactly one element of $S$, which is last in its specified order. Composition substitutes ordered fibres, concatenating them in the outer order; inputs sent to $*$ are discarded. Identity maps have singleton ordered fibres. A base arrow is inert if every non-basepoint of its target has exactly one preimage. Put $L=N(\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes})$ and let $A\subset L$ be the nerve of the full subcategory with $S=\varnothing$. The colour objects are $a=(\langle1\rangle,\varnothing)$ and $m=(\langle1\rangle,\{1\})$.

An operadic fibration over $L$ means a categorical fibration $r:\mathcal O\to L$ with cocartesian lifts of inert base arrows and the following Segal conditions. For $w=(\langle n\rangle,S)$, inert projection to each colour gives an equivalence $\mathcal O_w\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n\mathcal O_{c_i}$, where $c_i=m$ for $i\in S$ and $a$ otherwise. The empty product is terminal. For every base arrow $u:w\to z$ and $X\in\mathcal O_w$, $Y\in\mathcal O_z$, choose inert projections $Y\to Y_j$. Composition induces an equivalence from the space of arrows $X\to Y$ over $u$ to the product over output indices $j$ of the spaces of arrows $X\to Y_j$ over the corresponding composite $u_j$. An inert arrow of $\mathcal O$ is an $r$-cocartesian arrow above an inert base arrow. These conditions are properties of the given data, not assertions that such a fibration exists.

A coherent left tensoring of $\mathcal M$ over a monoidal infinity-category $\mathcal V$ of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is such an $r$ which is cocartesian over all arrows, with identified colour fibres $\mathcal O_a=\mathcal V$ and $\mathcal O_m=\mathcal M$. The pure-$a$ restriction encodes the specified monoidal structure: its restriction to the ordered consecutive-block maps is the nonsymmetric monoidal model of that definition. Transport of an ordered list of $a$ inputs to $a$ gives their tensor product; transport of an ordered list of $a$ inputs followed by one $m$ input to $m$ gives their action on that input. The empty list of $a$ inputs uses the unit. The operadic fibration and its coherent functors, rather than only binary products and equations in a homotopy category, are the specified action data. A weak enrichment uses the operadic fibration without requiring cocartesian lifts of all base arrows.

An associative algebra is an inert-preserving section $B:A\to\mathcal O|_A$. Coherent module objects are inert-preserving sections $H:L\to\mathcal O$, with coherent transformations over $L$ and all higher simplices; $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ is their strict simplicial fibre under restriction to $A$ over the given section $B$. Its underlying-object functor is evaluation at $m$. Here inert-preserving means carrying every inert base arrow to an inert arrow of $\mathcal O$.
